cnl-ckc knowledge base kb-2026-10-29-rc.1

This is a release candidate (a pre-release) of the cnl-ckc knowledge base. The clinical review of its content has not started. Use it to build and test software that reads the knowledge base. Do not use it to make clinical decisions. The README of https://github.com/eturkes/cnl-ckc describes the project.

## Download

Download the file **cnl-ckc-kb-only-2026-10-29-rc.1.tar.gz**. It holds the knowledge base and nothing else. The file **cnl-ckc-kb-only-2026-10-29-rc.1.tar.gz.sha256** holds its SHA-256 checksum. To check the download, put the two files in one directory and run `sha256sum -c cnl-ckc-kb-only-2026-10-29-rc.1.tar.gz.sha256` there. The output must report OK. GitHub adds the two "Source code" archives to every release. They hold the repository at this tag, and you do not need them to use the knowledge base.

## What the knowledge base is

cnl-ckc turns the text of published clinical guidelines into rules that software can query. Each covered passage of a guideline becomes a text in Attempto Controlled English (ACE). ACE is a restricted form of English that a clinician can read and compare with the passage. A compiler turns each ACE text into plain Prolog, so a standard Prolog system can load it.

This candidate holds one guideline: CDC Clinical Practice Guideline for Prescribing Opioids for Pain — United States, 2022 (MMWR Recomm Rep 2022;71(No. RR-3):1–95). cnl-ckc divides the guideline into 927 passages. 492 passages have their own ACE document, and 246 passages restate content that another document covers. 189 passages are not covered, because they hold no directive to compile: reports of third-party guidance or policy (77), context without a directive (58), the guideline's development process (29), aims (19) and headings (6). The file `data/guidelines/cdc-2022-opioid/coverage.tsv` in the archive gives the status and the reason for each passage.

## What the archive holds

To extract the archive, run `tar -xzf cnl-ckc-kb-only-2026-10-29-rc.1.tar.gz`. This makes the directory `cnl-ckc-kb-g673b3c1f3bfd/`, which is a BagIt bag. The name of the directory gives the commit that last changed the knowledge base.

- `data/guidelines/cdc-2022-opioid/pl/`: the Prolog file of each of the 492 documents.
- `data/guidelines/cdc-2022-opioid/ace/`: the ACE text of each document.
- `data/guidelines/cdc-2022-opioid/align/`: for each document, the links between parts of the ACE text and parts of the source passage.
- `data/guidelines/cdc-2022-opioid/queries/`: 6 prepared questions, with their answers and proof traces.
- `data/guidelines/cdc-2022-opioid/source/`: the guideline PDF and the text extracted from it.
- `data/guidelines/cdc-2022-opioid/README.md`: the source, the rights and the coverage of the guideline.
- `data/guidelines/schema.pl`: the comparison predicates that the documents use.
- `README-dist.md`: the full description of the contents and of the Prolog schema.
- `release-manifest.tsv`: the SHA-256 of each file and the review label of each document.
- `LICENSE` and `NOTICE`: the license terms.

## How to load it

You need SWI-Prolog. The project tests with version 10.0.2. In the extracted directory, load `schema.pl` first, then one or more documents:

```
swipl -q -s data/guidelines/schema.pl -s data/guidelines/cdc-2022-opioid/pl/cdc2022-opioid-rec01-imp01.pl
```

To load the whole guideline together with the facts of a patient, declare the schema predicates as tabled before the first document loads. The section "Loading a whole knowledge base" in `README-dist.md` gives the declaration. Without it, a broad question can fail to finish.

## Status of this candidate

- The review has not started. All 492 documents are unreviewed.
- A later candidate or the release can change the content.
- To use the knowledge base in other software, pin the release tag `kb-2026-10-29` when it exists.
- This tag replaces two earlier `kb-2026-10-29-rc.1` tags. The guideline files did not change. The first tag named commit e4c269780509c18603a0d50a079248be28d9fda3. Its archive had a different file name and a different `README-dist.md`, so its checksum is different. Its release also published the reviewer program, which this candidate does not publish. The second tag named commit aa489400269a741e3089edd9329c068143b69ba6. Its archive is identical to the archive of this tag, but its release had no checksum file. If you fetched an earlier tag, run `git fetch --tags --force`.

## How to verify the download

1. Check the download against the checksum file, as in "Download" above. This check finds a damaged download. It does not show who published the archive. Steps 2 and 3 show that.
2. In a clone of https://github.com/eturkes/cnl-ckc, check the signature of the tag. Run `git -c gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile=docs/allowed_signers verify-tag kb-2026-10-29-rc.1`. The output must report a good signature with the key fingerprint below.
3. In the directory of the download, check the archive against the checksum in the signed tag. Run `git -C <clone> tag -l --format='%(contents:body)' kb-2026-10-29-rc.1 | sha256sum -c --ignore-missing`. The archive must report OK. The other lines of these notes cause a warning about lines that are not checksums.
4. Extract the archive. In `cnl-ckc-kb-g673b3c1f3bfd/`, run `sha256sum -c manifest-sha256.txt tagmanifest-sha256.txt`. Each line must report OK.
